name: Lambert Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of proximal muscle weakness predominantly affecting lower limbs
Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes that improve with repeated muscle contraction
Detection of antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels
Incremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation electromyography testing
Presence of autonomic symptoms such as dry mouth or erectile dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of proximal muscle weakness, reduced deep tendon reflexes improving with exercise, and positive voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by electrophysiological studies and antibody testing; exclusion of myasthenia gravis is essential.

laboratory: Presence of anti-P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies
Elevated creatine kinase usually normal or mildly elevated
imaging: Chest CT or PET scan to identify underlying small cell lung carcinoma or other malignancies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; autoimmune etiology
other: Electromyography showing incremental response on high-frequency repetitive nerve stimulation
Improvement of muscle strength after exercise or 3,4-diaminopyridine administration

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies instead of calcium channel antibodies
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Predominantly ocular and bulbar weakness without autonomic symptoms
Genetic mutations affecting neuromuscular junction proteins

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Presence of paraneoplastic syndrome indicating underlying malignancy
Severe autonomic dysfunction causing orthostatic hypotension or arrhythmias
references: Oh SJ. Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome: Diagnosis and Treatment. Neurol Clin. 2018;36(2):361-374.
Orphanet: Lambert Syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
Drachman DB. Myasthenia Gravis. N Engl J Med. 1994;330(25):1797-1810.
